newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania trader slams Azomures tender sale.
newsitem.headline: Romania trader slams Azomures tender sale.

text.p: Romanian trader Omnimpex Chemicals SA, one of the two bidders for a majority stake in listed fertiliser maker Azomures SA, said on Monday it had appealed against the results of last week's tender sale.
Omnimpex lodged an appeal with the State Ownership Fund (FPS) contesting the way in which the bids had been assessed, a company statement showed.

The FPS, the former majority stockholder of Azomures, sold 51 percent of the company -- whose share capital stands at 209.5 billion lei -- to Romanian trading company Euro Trading Chemicals SRL last Tuesday.
The Fund announced the deal one day later arousing discontent among local capital market players, who said rules on listed companies' transparency had been breached.
Omnimpex said rivals Euro Trading had won the tender despite a lower bid. "We offered some 140 billion lei more than them," Ionel Baibarac, an Omnimpex adminstrator, said.

The FPS did not give an overall figure for the purchase by Euro Trading. Last week it said it had sold shares with a nominal value of 1,000 lei at 3,600, but on Monday FPS spokesman Viorel Ispas said the selling price was 90,000 lei per share with a face value of 25,000.
Azomures had a share split to 1,000 lei from 25,000 after oversubscription in a mass selloff. The FPS considered the face value before the split when it made the selloff, Ispas said.
Ispas said that Omnimpex had failed to appeal within the 24-hour deadline. "They had a full day to contest the results."
Omnimpex retorted that they had been given only one hour to lodge a complaint.

"Price was not the only issue considered when assessing the two bids," Ispas said. "We also had in view other pledges, including, in the case of Euro Trading, the equivalent of $38.7 million in five-year investment, higher wages for employees and fertiliser supply facilities for farmers."
Omnimpex said their commitments were similar.
"Euro Trading also has an association deal with Azomures staff, who get 10 percent of the stake it bought," Ispas said.
"Euro Trading already paid 10 percent of the value of the contract and it will be penalised if it fails to deliver on its pledges," he added.
